newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end sharply higher as fears of rate rise ease.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end sharply higher as fears of rate rise ease.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply higher on Friday as expectations of an imminent credit tightening receded after the release of weaker-than-expected April industrial output data on Thursday, traders said.

However, JGBs pared some earlier gains in afternoon trade after an official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) said he sees a chance of credit tightening by the early autumn, given improving economic fundamentals, they said.
The June ended at 124.01, up sharply from Thursday's close of 123.50. Turnover was 49,335 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.550 percent as of 0635 GMT, down from Thursday's close of 2.630 percent.
The June fell to the intra-day low of 123.62 in the afternoon due to the LDP official's comments, traders said.
Koji Omi, deputy chairman of the LDP's Policy Research Council, told Reuters: "There is a chance of an interest rate increase by early autumn as economic fundamentals are getting better."
The impact was limited, however, as Omi's comments were similar to those made by other politicians recently, a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.

JGBs were boosted by Japan's weaker-than-expected April industrial output data released on Thursday, which reassured the market that the Bank of Japan was unlikely to opt for an early credit tightening, a city bank trader said.

"Earlier, the BOJ's decision to push forward the release date of the next 'tankan' survey had led to some speculation that the central bank may raise interest rates immediately after the release of the key survey," the trader said.
Although the output data was not weak enough to rule out an interest rate rise by the end of the current business year, it helped ease fears of an early credit tightening, he said.
Having received reassurance from the output data, investors were detected buying long-term and medium-term cash bonds during the day, the city bank trader said.

"There was talk that (other) city banks were buying JGBs from the 190th to 196th issues in relatively large lots," the trader said. There was also talk of scattered buying by investors of medium-term JGBs, such as the 130th to 138th issues and the 140th to 149th issues, he added.
JGBs surged in morning trade, partly due to options-related buying ahead of the expiry of the June JGB futures options, traders said.

Those who had sold June JGB futures call options with a strike price of 124.00 earlier, built long positions in June JGB futures to hedge against the possibility of having the call options exercised against them, a dealer at a city bank's securities unit said.
Friday is the expiration date of the June JGB futures options.

Traders said JGBs were also supported by only limited rises in May Tokyo area consumer prices. The government said Tokyo prices rose 1.4 percent in May from a year earlier, while nationwide consumer prices prices for April rose 1.9 percent.
